title: Machine learning reveals two heterogeneous subtypes to assist immune therapy based on lipid metabolism in lung adenocarcinoma
summary: Machine-learning clustering of lung adenocarcinoma datasets identified lipid-metabolism and immune-active subtypes with different prognosis and progression patterns. A lipid-immune score predicted survival and retrospective immunotherapy response; these associations do not demonstrate prospective treatment benefit.
ai_technology: Consensus clustering and LASSO-derived lipid-immune score
organization: Southeast University; Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital, Tongji University

evidence.tested: Two subtypes were derived from 1,107 TCGA/GEO records; the study reports prognostic and immune associations and retrospective response prediction in external cohorts.
evidence.unknown: External cohorts are retrospective; predicted treatment sensitivity does not establish prospective response or treatment benefit.
evidence.ai_role: ConsensusClusterPlus/PAM clustering generated subtypes; a LASSO-derived lipid-immune score predicted survival and immunotherapy response.

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full-text Methods and Results; publication date and active/archive catalog comparison checked.
